title: Observability Governor service: enforce scrub, retention, and access-audit at ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: telemetry streams (traces, logs, metrics) currently apply inconsistent PII redaction and retention rules across SDKs and ingestion pipelines. That leads to support exposures, divergent retention behavior per tenant, and difficulty proving compliance.

Proposal: build an "Observability Governor" service that enforces telemetry governance decisions at ingest time: deterministic pseudonymization / tokenization, field-level scrubbing (regex + schema-aware), tenant-scoped retention enforcement, and mandatory RBAC access-audit logging. The Governor will be policy-driven (runtime rules), pluggable into the existing ingestion path (as a lightweight microservice in the dataplane with sidecar option), and expose admin APIs for policy lifecycle and data erasure requests. It will also provide SDK hooks so producers can surface structured annotations and opt into safe-debug tokens.

Goals: reduce PII leakage risk; provide a single source of truth for retention; emit immutable audit events for all telemetry accesses; minimize token-level latency overhead; preserve observability for debugging and model evals via reversible pseudonymization for authorized roles.
acceptance_criteria: All incoming telemetry can be evaluated by the Governor against tenant policies and, where applicable, transformed (scrubbed, pseudonymized, or dropped) before persisting to downstream stores.
Governor adds <20ms p95 wall-clock overhead to the ingestion path under typical load (validated in lab).
Audit log entries are produced for: policy evaluations, data erasure requests, and every administrative access to telemetry (format documented and immutable).
End-to-end regression suite with synthetic traces/logs proves identical downstream observability behavior for non-PII payloads and consistent redaction for PII examples.
Admin UI + API exist to create/update policy rules and to request a tenant data erasure with idempotent job tracking.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight Go service 'governord' deployed in ingestion path (Kafka consumer/proxy layer) with sidecar mode for Dedicated/Private deployments. Runtime policy engine evaluates rules expressed as JSON/YAML policy bundles stored in ConfigStore.

Policy language: support schema-aware selectors (JSONPath), regex, and field types (PII/ID/token). Policies may specify transform: redact / pseudonymize(HMAC+per-tenant salt) / truncate / drop / sample. Provide deterministic pseudonymization for debugging (HMAC with rotation window + key id).

SDK changes: add opt-in span/log annotation API so apps can mark fields as 'supportable' vs 'sensitive' to enable reversible tokens for SRE/SE with RBAC. Backwards-compatible default = conservative redaction. SDK change to be published in rust-go-python-js packages concurrently.

Performance: implement fast-path for messages that match 'no-policy' tenant or pre-approved schema. Continuous batching inside governor for throughput; use object pooling and precompiled regexes. Add CPU and latency budget targets to placement decisions.

Data model: preserve canonical metadata (tenant, span_id, trace_id) while scrubbing sensitive payload fields. For pseudonymized values include token_type and key_version in metadata for safe correlate. Avoid storing raw secrets in audit logs.

Audit format: newline-delimited JSON with stable schema (timestamp, tenant, event_type, object_id, policy_id, actor_id, outcome, op_id). Write audit stream to dedicated topic with retention and immutability enforced by storage layer.

Data erasure: expose POST /tenants/{t}/erase with job id; governor will schedule reindex jobs to tombstone or remove fields in downstream stores via connectors. Provide SLA and progress events to the Console.
RBAC: integrate with existing identity service for admin actions; Governor should reject admin API calls lacking required scopes and still emit audit traces for rejected attempts.
Privacy review: include KMS integration for HMAC key rotation; keys never leave HSM in Private deployments.
rollout_plan: Prototype: in-branch PoC that processes synthetic trace streams and applies two example policies (prod-default redaction, support-reversible for debug).
Integration tests: run against staging ingestion pipeline with preserved message rate and validate latency/throughput targets.
Feature-flagged canary: enable for 2% of TenantIDs in hosted region us-west-2; run both transform and 'passthrough + audit' comparison runs for 48h.
Canary evaluation: if audits and metrics pass, ramp 25% -> 75% -> 100% via feature flag over 2 weeks with rollback checkpoints.
Private/Dedicated: publish sidecar helm chart and runbook; offer migration helper to import existing tenant policies and keys.
Historical data: schedule optional backfill jobs (separate ticket) that apply transformations to archived indices with rate limits and clear progress tracking.
monitoring_slos: Governor ingress p95 additional latency < 20ms for 99% of messages (measured at ingress boundary).
Transformation errors < 0.01% of messages (excl. intentionally dropped messages).
Audit delivery success to audit-topic > 99.9% over 24h window.
CPU overhead per governor instance < 10% of current ingestion instance baseline under 2x nominal traffic.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Design review with PM (Lina Cho) and Security (Daniel Kim). Security requested deterministic pseudonymization audit and KMS-backed key metadata. Action: include key rotation window and key_id in tokens.
2026-02-27 - Engineering sync: Mateo proposed sidecar + centralized mode. Decision: implement both; start with centralized service for hosted, add sidecar for Dedicated/Private in parallel.
2026-03-05 - Spike results: PoC adds ~12ms p95 on synthetic 10k msg/s workload. Memory overhead nominal. Need to optimize regex engine for large schemas.
2026-03-09 - PM asked to add admin API for bulk policy imports; added to scope. Estimate increased from 5 -> 8 points.
2026-03-11 - Security review flagged audit retention policy; need to ensure audit-topic retention is immutable for 90 days for compliance. Added dependency to storage team (ENG-128271 follow-up).
